events.title: Our Lady of Guadalupe appears to Juan Diego
events.description: According to traditional Catholic accounts, an image of the Virgin Mary appeared imprinted on the cloak of Juan Diego, an Indigenous convert, near Mexico City. The cloak became the centerpiece of the Guadalupe devotion.
events.significance: The Guadalupe tradition became one of the most important Marian devotions in the world. December 12 is still celebrated each year as a major feast day across Mexico and Latin America.

events.title: Pennsylvania ratifies the U.S. Constitution
events.description: Pennsylvania's ratifying convention approved the new Constitution of the United States. It became the second state to do so, five days after Delaware.
events.significance: Pennsylvania's early approval gave momentum to the push for ratification in other states. That momentum helped the Constitution take effect as the nation's founding framework.

events.title: Marconi receives the first transatlantic radio signal
events.description: At Signal Hill in St. John's, Newfoundland, Guglielmo Marconi picked up a wireless signal sent across the Atlantic from England.
events.significance: The feat showed that radio waves could carry messages across oceans. It opened the way to modern global wireless communication.

events.title: Kenya wins independence from Britain
events.description: Kenya became an independent nation after decades of British colonial rule. The country's independence is still marked each December 12 as a national holiday.
events.significance: Kenya's independence was a milestone in the decolonization of Africa. It was led by Jomo Kenyatta, who went on to become the country's first president.
